subject: Multi-tenant failsafe zoning and egress playbook
messages:
From: Elena Torres <e.torres@summitfin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-17T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Summit RFP: network zoning + failure mode questions

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for taking Summit's security questionnaire. I've attached the set of items our reviewers flagged as high priority (sfp-security-questions.xlsx). We need concise, engineer-oriented answers for the following areas so we can move to procurement: 

- Multi-tenant zoning model: how tenants are isolated at the network and process levels; what controls prevent cross-tenant access.
- Failure modes: plausible cross-tenant blast-radius scenarios and the failsafe behaviors during instance/network failures.
- Egress and data exfiltration controls: default-deny posture, bastion/access patterns, and how outbound flows are audited.
- Evidence: diagrams, test artifacts, and any SOC/SLA statements that speak to availability and containment.

Can you provide a short technical summary and a topology diagram we can give to our network team by end of next week? If you prefer, we can book 30 minutes for a walkthrough.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Security Architect, Summit Financial
[Attachment: sfp-security-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@summitfin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Summit RFP: network zoning + failure mode questions

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is an initial topology sketch (mtf-zoning-v1.png) and below are concise, point-form answers we can expand during a call. Happy to convert any section into the format your procurement team prefers.

Multi-tenant zoning (high level):
- Control plane separated from inference runtime; control plane in a hardened management VPC, runtime in customer-configurable tenant VPCs/containers.
- Each tenant gets a logical namespace and dedicated application-layer tenancy (container/pod) with network policies enforcing namespace-level isolation.
- Sidecar proxies enforce per-tenant ACLs and mTLS between workloads; admin-plane services authenticate via RBAC tokens tied to customer tenant IDs.

Failure modes and failsafe behaviors:
- Instance failure: autoscaling replaces failed workers; KV cache is replicated across isolated failure domains to bound state exposure.
- Cross-tenant software fault: sidecar enforces memory+namespace boundaries; process crashes are limited to the local container, and requests are drained at the proxy to avoid request bleed.
- Network partition: routing policy prefers local-zone replicas; if unable to maintain SLA, system fails closed for affected tenant(s) and routes to a lower-capacity failover variant rather than a shared hot path.

Egress and exfiltration controls:
- Default-deny outbound at VPC/subnet level with whitelisted egress proxies.
- Customers may require a dedicated egress NAT or private peering; options: NAT per-tenant, centralized bastion egress with strict ACLs, or enforced proxy with DLP hooks.
- All outbound flows are logged at token-level; we retain flow metadata and per-token cost/latency traces for audit.

Monitoring, detection, and response:
- Per-tenant telemetry (metrics, traces, request logs) with alerting for anomalous volume/patterns.
- Canary traffic and rate-limited throttles to contain sudden spike-based abuse.

Attachments: topology sketch and a short packet describing isolation. Want to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next Tue/Wed?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mtf-zoning-v1.png (image/png)]

From: Elena Torres <e.torres@summitfin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Summit RFP: network zoning + failure mode questions

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the diagram. A few clarifying items from our reviewers (copied inline):

> Multi-tenant zoning (high level):...
- Reviewer: how do you guarantee tenant-by-tenant crypto material separation when control plane services are shared? Are keys per-tenant, KMS-backed?

> KV cache is replicated across isolated failure domains...
- Reviewer: what are the replication boundaries? Could a single storage replica contain multiple tenants' cache shards? If so, how is access controlled?

> Default-deny outbound...
- Reviewer: in a high-throughput inference environment (bursty token flows), how do you avoid increased latency when routing through a centralized bastion/proxy vs per-tenant NAT? Any measured overheads?

We attached a short risk outline with the specific questions the procurement team will use to score answers (summit-risk-outline.pdf). If you can answer these three items and provide a short mitigation table for each, that will cover most of our scoring criteria.

We can take the call if that helps; earliest availability is Thursday 09:00-10:00 PT.

Elena
[Attachment: summit-risk-outline.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@summitfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Summit RFP: network zoning + failure mode questions — consolidated answers and evidence pack

Elena —

Thanks for the follow-up and the risk outline. Below is a consolidated response addressing each of your reviewers' points, plus a compact mitigation table and links to evidence. We can review live in the Thursday slot if you prefer a walkthrough.

1) Tenant crypto material separation
- Keys: We use per-tenant envelope keys stored in the customer's configured KMS (cloud KMS or customer-managed HSM). Control plane stores only wrapped keys and never persists plaintext material.
- KMS separation options: supported models are (a) customer KMS per-tenant, (b) shared KMS with strict IAM scoping and audit logs, or (c) HSM-backed key-per-tenant for highest assurance.
- Evidence: KMS audit logs and HSM integration guide available on request.

2) KV cache replication boundaries and access controls
- Replication: cache shards are assigned to tenant-specific namespaces. Physical replication may co-reside on the same worker for capacity efficiency, but access enforcement is at the sidecar/proxy and runtime layer — no tenant identifier keys are accepted from outside the shard's namespace.
- Access control: sidecar enforces tenant-scoped ACLs; runtime verifies tenant id and token signature before serving cached entries. Cache read/write operations are logged with tenant and request id for auditability.

3) Egress path overhead and latency considerations
- Options & trade-offs: per-tenant NAT offers lower median latency (microbenchmark: ~0.5–2ms additional per-request), but increases operational cost and IP footprint. Centralized proxy/bastion simplifies policy and DLP integration but adds variable latency (~2–6ms observed in our benchmarks under typical traffic).
- Recommendation: provide both options — default to per-tenant egress for high-SLA customers, centralized proxy for customers needing consolidated DLP/legal inspection. Our routing policy can automatically select the lower-latency path when tenant SLAs require it.

Mitigation table (brief):
- Blast-radius (software bug): sidecar sandboxing + kernel namespace isolation; canary rollouts + automatic circuit breakers.
- Cross-tenant data visibility via cache: namespace-scoped shards + cryptographic tenant ids + audit logs.
- Unauthorized egress: default-deny + enforced proxy/NAT + token-level outbound logging + alerting on anomalous exfil patterns.

Monitoring & ops:
- Per-tenant telemetry exported to tenant-specific logging buckets; redacted shared metrics to avoid leakage.
- Anomaly detection hooks with playbooks to quarantine tenant routes and escalate to on-call.

Evidence pack and links:
- Final topology diagram (final-topology-diagram.svg) attached.
- Evidence archive with benchmark logs and sample KMS audit snippets (egress-evidence.zip).
- Walkthrough deck (drive link above) includes microbenchmarks and a short video of failover behavior.

If you'd like, we will prepare a short, one-page decision matrix comparing per-tenant NAT vs centralized proxy for your network team to include in the RFP response. Let us know if Thursday 09:00 PT still works; otherwise propose two windows and we'll adapt.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: final-topology-diagram.svg (image/svg+xml), egress-evidence.zip (application/zip)]
